reason: Accommodate the requested table and checklists under the existing byte gate. No CSS declarations changed here.
comments: /* ---------- Model flow stages (v4.4.5) ---------- The operator asked for this scene to follow an eight-stage mockup, and for four of that mockup's problems to be fixed rather than inherited. Three of the four are decisions about construction, and they are the reason this block has no tab, no ring, and no absolute position in it: - Its three prompt kinds and three output kinds were behind two tablists. A reader comparing three things cannot compare them one at a time, so both are plain lists. - Its stage 07 placed four labels around a ring by absolute offset and drew the arrows in a separate fixed viewBox, which is what "misplaced, text that can't be read" describes. Two unrelated coordinate systems cannot be nudged into agreement, so the passes are a line instead: `.mx-passes` is a grid, and overlap is not a state it can reach. - Its select, textarea, and buttons are static content here. Nothing waits to be operated. */

/* ---------- Harness work sequence and session trail (v4.4.5) ---------- From the operator's mockup. The work sequence is a plain ordered grid and the artifact chain is a flex row of chips, both for the same reason the rest of this plan keeps giving: the mockup positions its equivalents inside fixed viewBoxes, and a label placed by absolute offset is a label that will overlap something at a width nobody tested. Every chain selector is COMPOUND on purpose. `.hx-row span { display: block }` has two components and a lone `.hx-chain` has one, so the lone class loses on specificity and the chain stacks one chip per line at full width. That is what the first run of this phase shipped, and the test passed on it, because sorting four identical left offsets succeeds. */

/* v4.4.3: the comparison was two columns of prose, which asked the reader to hold four labelled sentences per lane in their head and compare them. The rebuild draws the thing that actually differs: which zones each lane can REACH. Both lanes show the same two zones, so the picture is the comparison and the words underneath only name what happens in each. A zone the lane cannot reach is marked with a dashed edge and a full-contrast label, never by dimming its text: the v4.4.2 contrast rule (BG-13, BG-14) applies to a state marker as much as to a sequence step. */
